5 تملّس : see مَلُسَ. ＝
-A2- It (a smooth thing) slipped forth from the hand [&c.]. (Har, p. 119.) ―
-b2- And hence, (Har, ubi supra,) (tropical:) He escaped; got away; or was, or became, or got, clear, quit, free, or at liberty; (S, * M, A, Msb, * K,) as also ↓ انملس , (S, A, K,) and ↓ إِمَّلَسَ , of the measure إِفْتَعَلَ, [or rather إِنْفَعَلَ,] and ↓ املاسّ ; (K;) مِنَ الأَمْرِ from the thing or affair; (S, A, TA;) and مِنْ يَدِى from my hand. (A.) ―
-b3- [Hence,] تملّس مِنَ الشَّرَابِ (assumed tropical:) He recovered from the wine. (AHn, M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
